balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs. Film rights amortisation is overlaid for reference -- it is the content cost already charged above the operating-income line, not a separate deduction.

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: the three profit lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom; amortisation of licensed and self-produced film/TV content (RMB1,980.6m in FY2023, RMB866.6m in FY2024) is one of the largest single costs behind cost of revenue and is -- unlike the fair-value swing below -- a real, recurring cost of the content business that the DCF does not add back.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income -- for Ruyi this gap is mostly the fair-value swing on investments, see the chart below
  • Film rights amortisation trending with or against content revenue

fairValueSwing.title: Fair-value swing vs adjusted net profit
fairValueSwing.content:
Net income (reported) is the statutory bottom line including every fair-value mark. Adjusted net profit is China Ruyi's own non-GAAP measure that strips out other gains/(losses) -- net, the line carrying fair-value remeasurement of its large investment portfolio (stakes in other listed and unlisted media/tech businesses).

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: the investment book swung from a RMB1,222.0m loss in FY2024 to a RMB1,281.7m gain in FY2025 -- a RMB2,503.7m swing that alone explains why reported net income went from -190.5m to +1,796.6m while adjusted net profit rose far more steadily (1,065.0m to 1,962.6m). The DCF values the business on adjusted net profit / owner FCF, not the reported figure, because these marks are non-cash, non-operating and have no reliable sign from year to year.

What to watch:

  • Other gains/(losses) swinging the sign of reported net income while adjusted net profit keeps growing
  • Whether the investment book is shrinking as a share of the balance sheet (less future earnings noise) or growing (more)
  • Adjusted net profit itself still includes items beyond the film/TV/streaming/games core -- treat it as a cleaner but not perfect proxy

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China Ruyi Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
